description.value: The Original Fort Langley Site marks the location where the Hudson's Bay Company first established Fort Langley in 1827 at Derby Reach on the Fraser River, before the fort was relocated inland to its present site in 1840. Designated as part of Canada's national historic site network, this monument commemorates the origins of one of BC's most significant fur-trade era landmarks. The site sits within the broader Fraser Valley cycling corridor, making it of interest to history-minded touring cyclists passing through the Lower Mainland.
